# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👈]

I need to understand these gestures from Mute first. Let me think about what they could mean.

Mute can see the manual and is sending me paired gestures. Since I can't hear anything and Mute can't speak, this is likely Mute establishing a code - perhaps pairing numbers with attributes, or trying to map wire numbers to something.

The pairs are: [☝ 👍], [✌ 🖐], [🤟 👆], [✋ 👇], [👌 👈]

This looks like it could be a numbering scheme: ☝(1) ✌(2) 🤟(3) ✋(4)... wait, but paired with others. Possibly Mute is establishing "1=👍(good/safe), 2=🖐(?), 3=👆(?), 4=👇(?), 5=👈(?)" — trying to tag each wire number with a status.

I don't have enough context yet to decode this confidently. I should not act on the bomb (I can't anyway), but I should respond to help build a shared code. Since I go last in the turn order (Blind, Mute, Deaf), I've now seen Mute's gestures this round. I should report what I see on the bomb to Mute (since Mute can't see) and to Blind isn't reachable by me directly for speech... wait, I can speak and both Mute and Blind receive speech from me.

Let me report the bomb state clearly to both, and acknowledge I received gestures but need clarification via a system where Mute can teach me a code using gestures (I see gestures, good).

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb shows: display reads 0, light is blue, five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, I saw your gesture pairs but do not know their meaning yet - please establish a code, for example gesture a wire number then a symbol for cut or safe.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍]

Mute sent [✋ 👍]. Earlier Mute sent pairs that could be establishing a numbering code: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✋=4, 👌=5 (using standard finger-counting gesture progression), each paired with a second symbol possibly meaning something about that wire (👍=good/safe, 🖐=?, 👆=?, 👇=?, 👈=?).

If ✋=4 and now Mute pairs it with 👍 (thumbs up = good/safe), that could mean "wire 4 is safe" or "cut wire 4". This matches my earlier report where wire 4 is yellow.

I should acknowledge understanding and ask for confirmation, and relay to Blind since Blind can't see gestures at all and needs the info verbally from someone who can hear... but I can't hear Mute either. Only Blind can hear Mute. So I don't need to relay Mute's gestures - Blind already hears Mute directly if Mute speaks, but Mute can't speak! Mute can only gesture (which I see) or... wait Mute "cannot speak" per the table. So Mute's only channel is gesture, which only I (Deaf) can see. So I must relay!

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute gestured to me: symbol four (shown as a fist with pinky-ring-middle down, index+thumb sequence) paired with thumbs-up, likely meaning wire 4 is safe or should be cut. Wire 4 is yellow. Waiting for more confirmation before you act.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute now sent the same symbols but separately: [✋] then [👍]. This confirms these are two distinct signals, not one combined gesture — reinforcing that ✋ likely means "4" (wire 4) and 👍 means "safe/correct/go ahead", sent as separate confirmations after presumably hearing something from Blind (who speaks and Mute can hear).

This suggests Mute and Blind have been communicating via speech (Blind speaks, Mute hears), and Mute is now relaying to me via gesture that wire 4 is confirmed safe to cut. I should pass this confirmation to Blind as reinforcement.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute repeated the signal as two separate gestures: four, then thumbs-up. This looks like confirmation - wire 4 (yellow) is the one to cut. If you've heard anything different from Mute directly, prioritize that, but this is what I'm seeing.")
```
